title: Charge capital gains tax on leaving the UK and at death
shortTitle: CGT on leaving and at death
noun: capital gains tax on leaving and at death
headline: Gains on leaving and at death, taxed from 2028-29: RF’s £4bn for both.
description: Today any gain built up on an asset is wiped out for capital gains tax when its owner dies: the heir inherits it at its value at death and pays nothing on the gain that came before. Someone who leaves the UK before selling pays no British capital gains tax on the gain built up while they lived here either. The Resolution Foundation proposes taxing both: the full gain when the heir eventually sells, and a settling-up charge on people who leave the country. It puts the two together at £4 billion a year, and this card is that package at that figure. The Centre for the Analysis of Taxation puts the gains tax forgone on business owners who emigrate alone at £0.5 billion a year or more, which the leavers' card carries. The business department has ruled out a corporate exit tax; a personal charge on people who leave has not been ruled out. It is grown with the OBR's capital gains tax forecast from 2029-30.

baselinePolicy.text: Gains are rebased to market value on death and the built-up gain is never charged to capital gains tax (the estate may pay inheritance tax instead), and someone who leaves the UK before selling pays no British capital gains tax on the gain. Capital gains tax receipts are forecast at £32.0bn in 2029-30.

source.quote: when assets are held until death, any built-up gains are written off for tax purposes

alreadyIncludes: The October 2024 rise in the main rates to 18% and 24% (Autumn Budget 2024, Table 5.1 line 27).

earliestStart.text: Capital gains tax on a year’s gains is paid by 31 January after the tax year, so a change from April 2027 shows almost entirely from 2028-29: the October 2024 rate rise scored £90m in 2024-25 and £1.4bn in 2025-26.

sources.quote: You must report by 31 December in the tax year after you made your gain and pay by 31 January.
Increase the main rates of CGT to 18% and 24% from 30 October 2024

terms.label: Resolution Foundation estimate for ending the death write-off together with an exit charge

source.quote: The combination of these two measures would raise an estimated £4 billion a year

rawSource.note: The Foundation's £4bn a year is taken as a 2029-30 steady-state figure and moved with the OBR's capital gains tax receipts to the other years. It is the Foundation's figure for both measures together, as this card is. Nothing is counted before 2028-29: see earliestStart.

caveats: An upper bound by construction: the Resolution Foundation costs the death write-off and an exit charge together and publishes no split. Nobody has certified either figure.

Timing: the Foundation's proposal taxes the gain when the heir eventually sells, so revenue would build up over years, not arrive in full at once. The card applies the steady-state figure from 2028-29, the first year in which tax on 2027-28 disposals is paid.
Static: people would hold, gift or restructure assets differently once gains at death were taxed, and would bring disposals forward before the change, as they did before the October 2024 rate rise.

considerations.text: The write-off at death creates what the Foundation calls perverse incentives to avoid realising gains; removing it changes when people sell, give and die holding assets. The OBR notes that capital gains tax receipts rose about 60% in 2025-26 as disposals were brought forward ahead of the October 2024 rate rise, so the yield of any single year would differ sharply from the steady state.

sources.quote: This creates perverse incentives to avoid realising gains

considerations.text: The Foundation describes the write-off as a particularly valuable tax concession to those with very large business wealth. Estates that pay inheritance tax already bear a charge on the same assets; how the two taxes would interact is a design choice this card does not make.

sources.quote: a particularly valuable tax concession to those with very large business wealth

interactions.text: Both reach assets passing at death. Charging capital gains at death and inheritance tax on the same estate is a double charge unless one is set against the other; neither figure allows for the other.
A higher rate on gains also raises what the death write-off is worth, and so what ending it yields; the £4bn is at today's rates.
This package already charges people who leave: together they count it twice.
